# Brimholt repository instructions

- Brimholt is an original working name, not verified trademark/name clearance. Do not reuse proprietary Tibia artwork, maps, names, or code.
- Use Godot 4.5+, typed GDScript, and native ENet/MultiplayerAPI. No Node server, third-party APIs, paid services, or downloaded game assets.
- Open Tibia engines are high-level references, not dependencies: do not copy/translate GPL code without a licensing decision; MIT reuse needs file/dependency checks and applicable notices. Neither source license licenses proprietary Tibia assets. See README.md.
- The world is `game/maps/overworld.tscn`, painted in Godot's TileMap editor (terrain custom data, plus Spawns/Ferrymen/Items markers). Treat that scene as the source of truth; do not regenerate it with `tools/make_map.gd --force` without the user's approval.
- The game is a small LAN prototype for up to twelve players (Knight, Paladin, Sorcerer, Druid vocations): original 32-pixel tile map, cardinal grid movement, collision, smooth presentation, host/join, visibly equipped items, a flat backpack with ground items and drag-and-drop, eight equipment slots with item stats, a 256×256 world with a western coast of ferry ports and one inland lake whose island (Blackreed Isle) is a level 40-50 PvP hunting zone, and level 1-50 balance curves anchored on a 350,000-health final boss that needs a ten-player, all-vocation raid (`game/balance.gd`, `docs/balance.md`).
- Derive new mob, item, and progression numbers from `game/balance.gd` rather than inventing standalone values; regenerate `docs/balance.md` with `tools/balance_table.gd` when constants change.
- Combat is Tibia-style and server-authoritative in `game/combat.gd` (target lock, 2 s auto-attacks, spells with own and group cooldowns, monster aggro/leash/respawn, experience shared by damage, 10% death penalty with classic item loss, white/red skulls, PvP only in PvP zones). Derive monster and spell numbers from `game/balance.gd`; never trust clients with damage, health, or experience.
- Run `python3 tools/playtest.py --godot godot` after gameplay changes that affect the main loop; read its findings, not just pass/fail.
- Keep nested containers, loot tables and trading, blessings, procedural caves, floor systems, persistence/authentication, and AI or dialogue-driven NPCs out unless the user selects them as a milestone. Ferrymen are static, menu-driven NPCs.
- NPC interaction is a right-click context menu of services (Travel now; Buy and Quests later), never Tibia-style typed keywords. Add new services to that menu.
- Player input goes through `game/keybinds.gd`: never hard-code gameplay keys. New actions need a default binding there; the action bar has nine rebindable slots (default 1-9) whose entries come from `Keybinds.BAR_ACTIONS` (spells go there once combat exists).
- Peer 1 owns all gameplay state. Keep input ownership separate from node multiplayer authority. Validate RPC senders; clients request actions, never positions or authoritative appearance.
- Enforce movement timing, walkability, occupancy, item moves (reach, slot type, capacity, cooldown), and player limits on the server. Synchronize spawn, late-join, equipment, ground-item, and disconnect state reliably; send backpack contents only to their owner.
- Preserve host/client behavior parity. Art is original sprite sheets in `assets/sprites` (see README "Art and sprites"): one layered sheet per worn item, never a sprite per combination, and no downloaded or Tibia-derived assets.
- Inspect actual files and reuse existing helpers before editing. Make surgical changes, keep types explicit, and surface errors.
- Consult the relevant repository skill before gameplay, networking, equipment, or validation work.
- Check tooling before claiming results. Use bounded checks, report what actually ran, and never bypass denied permissions.
- Keep registered checkout paths stable. Do not publish a repository, add a remote, or install system-wide tools without authorization.
